scope: Bounded normal-operation acceptance of the unchanged Level 8 implementation. No fault injection. Not a statement of fault tolerance, production readiness or availability.
overall_reason: P4-r1, P4-r2, P4-r3: generator_validity FAIL (burst stream scheduling-lag p99 above 10 ms under the frozen literal rule); each run's prediction p95 comparison is therefore NOT VERIFIED.
P5-r1: soak_memory_growth_le_32MiB FAIL as measured. The measurement is confounded by a defect in the scratch instrumentation (see soak_memory_assessment); the frozen result is retained.

instrumentation.observer: separate docker exec python (container uid 0, same user as service, not privileged): fd identities/classes, thread ids/names, all processes, cgroup memory; no monitoring HTTP

plan.observation: 8 s idle after reference; baseline = third of three identical fd+thread identity sets 1 s apart (max 10); drain+0, +5, +15; one GET /health closed by client; probe+0, +1, +5; stop sampler; SIGTERM to uvicorn; list processes 2 s after its exit; remove container
plan.fd_rule: per role: PASS if no non-baseline identity at probe+5; else FAIL if one identity is present at all of drain+15, probe+0, +1, +5; else NOT VERIFIED
plan.thread_rule: AnyIO allowance from L8-2D C2: parent PASS if count at probe+5 <= baseline+2; worker and tracker <= baseline; else FAIL if a new tid is present at all four post-drain points and count stays above allowance at all of them; else NOT VERIFIED
plan.leak_rule: after uvicorn exit no non-zombie parent, worker, tracker or python process
plan.clean_shutdown: uvicorn exit 0 or 143 (SIGTERM re-raised when not PID 1), shutdown messages, probe record, no Traceback, <=15 s
plan.memory: peak <= 90% of 1 GiB (max cgroup memory.peak and samples, includes observer/sampler). P5 growth = median memory.current over last 60 s of measurement minus median over first 60 s, <=32 MiB, >=40 samples each
plan.baseline: median of the three P0 measurement prediction latency_attempted_all_terminal p95; requires all three generator-valid, reconciled, 100% success; else comparisons NOT VERIFIED. P1,P2,P4,P5 limit baseline+max(20%,5 ms)
plan.generator_validity: every open-loop stream including the P4 burst stream (harness open_loop=true): exact scheduled count, 0 missed, scheduling-lag p99<=10 ms separately for warm-up and measurement, 0 outstanding. The burst reading is the literal one; the smoke burst of 24 showed burst lag p99 13.7 ms before this freeze and no exemption is made
plan.attribution: generator failure stays FAIL; that run's prediction p95 degradation, explanation p95 and P2 95% success gates become NOT VERIFIED (numbers retained); direct correctness, lifecycle and resource observations keep PASS/FAIL
plan.error_classification: unexpected operational error = any non-success, except correctly formed 503 explanation_overloaded (fixed body, Retry-After 1, no-store) in P2 and P4
plan.cohorts: harness cohort from analytical arrival index; analyzer checks index<warm count
plan.overall: PASS only if all 14 complete, every applicable mandatory gate PASS, regression, flat-image and serial verification pass, preservation passes; any FAIL => FAIL; else any NOT VERIFIED => NOT VERIFIED. No replacement runs

observations: P4-r1 prediction p95 was 13.188 ms against a limit of 13.122 ms (delta 5.066 ms): numerically above the limit by 0.066 ms. The frozen attribution rule makes the gate NOT VERIFIED; the number is not discounted.

All three P4 runs: burst-stream lag p99 19.7-21.7 ms; the prediction stream in the same runs stayed within 10 ms. The lag is the delay in starting 32 tasks released together. Historical L8-2D validity checks cited for P4 applied to the prediction workload with a 5 ms limit.
P4 burst outcomes: 19/13, 16/16, 18/14 success/overload; every overload used the fixed envelope, Retry-After 1 and no-store; queue high water 8, admitted 9.

soak_memory_assessment.instrumentation_defect: The scratch wrapper appended every dispatcher Job to a list never cleared. Job holds its payload and future, and a completed future keeps its result, so the parent retained every explanation result for the lifetime.
soak_memory_assessment.historical_context: The L8-2D P5 record shows about 386 MiB post-readiness and 390 MiB post-drain under the same named profile, with different instrumentation. Not a controlled comparison.
soak_memory_assessment.attribution: The wrapper retention is a likely major or sole contributor. This is NOT established: no control run was made and none was authorized. Whether the unchanged service meets the 32 MiB limit is not established by this run. No production defect is established.
soak_memory_assessment.other_effects: The same retention was present in all 14 runs and also in the earlier L8-2DS and L8-2DSV wrappers; it adds to memory figures and may add garbage-collection work. Its effect on latency was not measured.

limitations: One shared host; fixed run order; CPU quotas are not dedicated cores.
All primaries were instrumented (wrapper, supervisor shell, memory sampler, external observer); overhead was not measured and latencies are not equivalent to uninstrumented ones.
The observer ran as the container's uid 0 without added privilege; snapshots are discrete.
Per-response checks are those of the committed generator; model identity, logit and attributions were checked by one reference request per lifetime and by the flat-image tests, not on every response.
Dispatcher capacity and counters come from the in-process wrapper.
httpx transitive dependencies are not hash-locked.

recommended_next_action: Do not treat Level 8 as operationally accepted. No production correction is justified by this evidence.

Review separately, for any future frozen plan only: whether a synchronized burst should be held to the open-loop 10 ms lag rule, or have its own predeclared launch-spread rule. No retrospective relaxation.

If separately authorized: fix the scratch wrapper to keep counts, not Job objects, and predeclare any new soak. P4 prediction latency also needs attention because one run was numerically above its limit.

instrumentation_retention.retaining_collection: module-level list JOBS (JOBS.append on every accepted submit), never cleared; EV was a second unbounded list of small event records
instrumentation_retention.retained_objects: dispatcher Job objects, each referencing its input payload and its concurrent.futures.Future; a completed future references its Outcome and result content
instrumentation_retention.lifecycle: without the list the dispatcher and request handler drop their references after completion; the list kept a strong reference until process exit, so nothing reachable from a Job could be released
instrumentation_retention.correction: scalar counters, deques bounded at 32 failure and 64 admission events, a generation set bounded by restart policy, a last-request-id scalar, and a future done-callback that references nothing
instrumentation_retention.other_collections_checked: wrapper holds no other growing collection; access log disabled; memory sampler streams to the host; the observer is a short-lived process; the generator shim keeps only distinct non-200 bodies in the generator process

burst_assessment.observation: All three follow-up bursts exceeded the limit, as did all three in L8-2DA and both 24-request smoke bursts. With the generator unchanged in this environment it has not met this requirement in any observed burst; this does not show it never can.
burst_assessment.distinctions: task start lag, HTTP connection acquisition (not observed) and server admission (wrapper timestamps) are different quantities. First server admission was about 22-36 ms and last about 205-236 ms after the scheduled instant, so requests did not reach admission simultaneously; the cause of that spread was not measured.
burst_assessment.prediction_numeric_exceedance: none of the three follow-up P4 prediction p95 values exceeded the follow-up limit; their formal gates remain NOT VERIFIED

corrected_soak_assessment.statement: Independent evidence that the tested service configuration met the memory-growth requirement in this 300 s soak under corrected instrumentation.
corrected_soak_assessment.limits: A small upward trend (30 s cgroup medians 386.7 to 388.8 MiB; parent RSS 267.1 to 268.8 MiB) continued to the end and is not characterized; one five-minute run does not establish long-run boundedness. It does not prove the defect caused every byte of the earlier 114.07 MiB growth. Cgroup figures include sampler and observer; process RSS values overlap and are not summed.

limitations: One shared host, fixed order, instrumented execution; overhead not measured.
Discrete resource snapshots; observer is container uid 0 without added privilege and shares service quotas.
P1, P2 and P3 were not repeated; their evidence is L8-2DA's, collected with the retaining wrapper (effect on latency not measured).
L8-2DS, L8-2DSV and L8-2DA memory observations remain confounded.
httpx transitive dependencies are not hash-locked.
recommendation: Do not declare L8-2 operationally accepted: the follow-up is FAIL and L8-2DA remains FAIL on the original contract.

Combined evidence shows no service-side correctness, lifecycle or corrected-memory gate failure in these runs; the remaining failures are generator burst-launch validity, which leaves P4 prediction latency formally unverified. No production correction is justified.
Any different burst contract needs a new explicit decision, defined in advance, and cannot satisfy the original contract retroactively.
